title: Live Traffic Probe Escrow and Decisioning Runbook
author: Aisha Kapoor
body:
Overview

Purpose: This runbook describes the Live Traffic Probe Escrow pattern and the decisioning matrix used to gate rollouts, trigger automatic fallbacks, and escalate regression triage when production-quality deltas are detected. The escrow pattern minimises risk from noisy short-term signals by holding a deterministic sample of traffic and its probes in an immutable store before they can influence automated rollouts.

Scope
- Applies to: Redwood-hosted models (public API routes), Dedicated model pools, and Private deployments that integrate the probe SDK.
- Not covered: offline batch evals, manual A/B experiments run entirely outside the Redwood serving runtime.

Quick summary
- Probe escrow holds (N) raw request+response records for 72 hours in s3://escrow-prod-probes/{model}/{date}.
- Gate checks run on escrowed data every 15m and produce a pass/fail decision with a confidence score.
- Failures trigger staged rollback: (1) local quant-fallback, (2) canary shrink to 0.1% traffic, (3) full rollback to prior model version if unresolved for 30m.

Owners and contacts
- Runbook owner: Model Reliability (model-reliability@redwood.com) — primary: Aisha Kapoor
- Oncall escalation: ML-runtime SRE (pager: #ml-runtime-oncall)
- Product owner for rollout policy: Priya Das (product)

Signals and telemetry contract
- Required metrics produced by the escrow pipeline (every probe emits these keys):
  - probe_id (string)
  - tenant_id (string)
  - model_version (string)
  - route (string)
  - timestamp_utc (ISO8601)
  - input_token_count (int)
  - output_token_count (int)
  - latency_ms (p95/p50 per-probe aggregated)
  - coherence_score (float, 0–1) — evaluator micro-metric scoring intent preservation
  - semantic_change_score (float, 0–1) — measured against baseline embedding similarity
  - safety_violations (int) — count of sentinel hits (see sentinel catalog)
  - quant_fallback_flag (bool)

Thresholds and SLOs (defaults)
- Latency tail: p99 latency increase > 35% relative to baseline (last 24h) -> alert candidate
- Coherence regression: median coherence_score drops by >= 6 percentage points on escrow samples -> fail gate
- Semantic drift: mean semantic_change_score decrement >= 0.12 over 1h window -> fail gate
- Safety violations: any increase of +5 violations / 1000 probes vs baseline -> immediate fail and page SRE
- Confidence requirement: decisions must meet min_confidence >= 0.7 (see Decision Confidence section)

Probe Escrow workflow (step-by-step)
1. Traffic sampling: router applies deterministic 1-in-K sampling keyed by tenant_id + route to ensure reproducibility.
2. Probe synthesis: each sampled request is wrapped with a probe signature and shadowed to the probe SDK.
3. Escrow write: SDK writes serialized record to escrow S3 path with encryption and manifest entry.
4. Preflight enrichment: enrichment lambda augments records with embeddings, baseline similarity, and micro-eval hooks.
5. Gate evaluation: gate runner pulls manifest in 15m batches, computes delta metrics against baseline and emits a gate_decision JSON to the decision topic.
6. Decision action: decision consumer applies action policy (no-op, notify, throttled-fallback, rollback).

Decision Confidence
- We compute a composite confidence score using three factors (weighted): sample stability (40%), signal-to-noise (30%), and historical sensitivity (30%).
- Minimum pass threshold: 0.70. Between 0.55–0.70 -> triage flag (human review). Below 0.55 -> automatic rollback for safety-flagged failures.

Decision matrix (summary table)
- Pass & high confidence: continue rollout, post to /release-events, no action.
- Fail & high confidence: trigger rollback step 1 (local quant-fallback) and page ML-runtime oncall.
- Fail & medium confidence: reduce canary traffic to 0.1% and create a triage ticket with attached escrow sample (5 examples).
- Safety violation (any confidence): immediate full rollback to previous pinned model and create SEV ticket.

Operational run commands and examples
- Manually re-run gate for a date range (CLI):
  rwn-escrowctl evaluate --model redwood-v2 --from 2025-01-05T00:00Z --to 2025-01-05T01:00Z --batch-size 5000

- Example gate_decision JSON (published to kafka topic decision.gates):
  {
    "model_version": "redwood-v2.17",
    "window_start": "2025-01-05T00:00:00Z",
    "window_end": "2025-01-05T00:15:00Z",
    "metrics": {"coherence_delta": -0.07, "semantic_delta": -0.13},
    "confidence": 0.82,
    "decision": "rollback-step-1"
  }

Telemetry retention and privacy
- Escrowed probe payloads are retained for 72 hours by default, then moved to a 365-day restricted archive only if tagged for regulatory review.
- Sensitive fields (PII) must be redacted at the SDK before escrow write. The SDK supports deterministic redaction rules and a redaction log.

Canary orchestration and rollback sequence
1. Local quant-fallback: switch the canary to run quantized variant with the same model name (fast fallback, < 30s config apply).
2. Canary shrink: reduce canary to 0.1% traffic for verification window (30m).
3. Hot swap: if failures persist, route canary traffic to previous model_version and mark current model as quarantined.
4. Full rollback: automated full-traffic revert after 30 minutes of unresolved fail state OR immediately if safety violation.

Debugging and triage playbook (for oncall)
1. Confirm artifact: verify model_version, commit hash, and build manifest (rwn-manifest show --model <model_version>).
2. Pull escrow sample: escrowctl fetch --model <model_version> --window <window_start>-<window_end> --limit 50 
3. Run local evaluator: docker run redwood/eval:latest --input sample.json --metric coherence --seed 42
4. Compare embeddings: use the baseline embedding snapshot (s3://baseline-embeds/{model}/snapshot-YYYYMMDD) and run: embed-diff --left escrow-embeds.json --right baseline.json --threshold 0.12
5. If service-level failure, escalate to ML-runtime SRE and attach gate_decision and top 10 escrow samples.

Post-incident activities
- Within 24h: owner files an incident summary and updates the triage ticket with root cause hypotheses.
- Within 72h: if RCA indicates model quality regression, schedule a model regression test in the eval harness and a targeted retrain or prompt-fix patch.
- Within 7 days: update the baseline snapshot if the new behavior is accepted, or deprecate model version and document mitigation steps.

Safety and audit notes
- All escrow writes are logged with write-id and stored under kms-encrypted S3 buckets.
- Access to escrow manifests is restricted to model-reliability and ML-runtime-SRE roles.

Appendix: example escrow schema (newline-delimited JSON)
- One line per probe record, minimal fields shown:
  {"probe_id":"p-abc123", "tenant_id":"t-45", "model_version":"redwood-v2.17", "route":"/chat/v1", "input":"<redacted>", "output":"<redacted>", "metrics":{"latency_ms":320,"coherence_score":0.71}}

Related pages and references

- Quant shadow guide: /applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quant-shadow-cohort-strategy-and-rollback-playbook-2026

Change history
- 2024-11-12: Created by Aisha Kapoor
- 2025-01-09: Clarified confidence thresholds and added CLI examples (reviewers: Liam Chen, Sofia Martinez)

Operational checklist (one-line)
- Is escrow enabled for this deployment? (yes/no)
- Are redaction rules applied? (yes/no)
- Has baseline snapshot been refreshed in the last 7 days? (yes/no)

End of runbook
